column2: The ground floor of a row of old Williamsburg Brooklyn tenements under the elevated train at night: steel roll down shutters covered in hot pink, orange and electric blue eye flower graffiti and tags, a bodega window lettered NEW YORKERS with fruit crates, a tenement doorway with a column of buzzers, wheat pasted posters of eye flowers, a typed notice taped to a door, sodium streetlight, wet sidewalk along the bottom edge.

The wall of an old Brooklyn tenement entrance hall: pressed tin wainscot painted dark green up to waist height, cracked cream plaster above with water stains, a long row of small numbered brass mailboxes stuffed with envelopes, a cork notice board with typed notices, scratched eye flower graffiti, an old cast iron radiator, light from one bare bulb.

A tenement corridor wall covered top to bottom in a vivid graffiti mural of giant flowers with a human eye at the centre of each, in hot pink, orange, yellow, cyan and electric blue on deep night blue, spray paint drips, tags reading N3W and MLOW, a numbered apartment door painted over with the mural, scuffed along the bottom, cold fluorescent light.

The wall of a century old railroad apartment in Williamsburg: layers of patterned wallpaper peeling away in big curls to show older wallpapers beneath (a faded 1920s rose pattern, a 1960s mustard geometric, and on top a cream paper with small blue eye flower motifs), cracked plaster, a dark wood picture rail, pale ghost rectangles where picture frames used to hang, an old push button light switch, warm lamp light.

A wall in a shabby Brooklyn landlord's office: dark wood panelling covered with rows and rows of old brass and steel keys hanging on little hooks, each with a paper tag and a number, framed property deeds, a wall calendar, a big map of Brooklyn blocks stuck with red pins, a nicotine stained ceiling line.

A wall of an old New York City housing court corridor: institutional two tone paint, pale green below and cream above, a long worn oak bench along the bottom, bulletin boards crammed with typed notices, calendars and court schedules, a round wall clock, a red fire extinguisher cabinet, a numbered courtroom door with a small wired glass window, scuff marks.

A tenement rooftop parapet and stair bulkhead at night: weathered red brick with hot pink and blue eye flower tags, a dented steel bulkhead door, a satellite dish, a string of warm bulbs, tar flashing along the bottom, the deep blue night sky above with a glow of city light.
